programme: SMARCB1 and SMARCE1 are core, mutually-targeting subunits of the SWI/SNF (BAF) chromatin-remodeling complex — SMARCE1's own target list is SMARCA4/SMARCB1/MYOG, i.e. its complex partners. SMARCB1 in turn targets GLI1 (the Hedgehog pathway effector) while MEIS3 targets SHH itself, and PRDM10, POU6F2 and SMARCB1 all converge directly on CDKN2A. YAP1, the Hippo effector known for cross-talk with BAF-complex activity and Hedgehog-driven programs, sits alongside this group. Together these six factors describe a BAF-complex/Hedgehog-Hippo module gating the CDKN2A (INK4a/ARF) checkpoint.
role_in_a: In COVID-19 this module would be expected to act through stress/inflammation-induced cellular senescence — BAF-complex and Hippo-YAP1 activity feeding CDKN2A induction is a plausible route to the p16-driven senescent, pro-inflammatory endothelial and immune-cell states reported in severe disease — but nothing in the retrieved material documents this for COVID-19 specifically.
role_in_b: In Lower_Grade_Glioma, CDKN2A status (homozygous deletion vs. intact) is a primary molecular determinant of tumor grade and outcome, and YAP1 is independently documented here as a prognostic biomarker and gene-network hub across cancers including glioma; BAF complexes (SMARCB1/SMARCE1) and Hedgehog-GLI1 signaling are established regulators of glioma/glioma-stem proliferation.
shared_axis: If both diseases route stress or oncogenic signaling through the same BAF-complex/Hippo-Hedgehog control of the CDKN2A checkpoint, the axis could appear concordant in both blood and brain cohorts even though nothing ties the two diseases together directly — COVID-19 via acute stress-induced senescence, LGG via chronic loss of the same checkpoint during tumor progression.
reasoning: YAP1's role in glioma/pan-cancer biology is independently documented by four retrieved papers, and the BAF-complex/Hedgehog convergence on CDKN2A is visible directly in the target lists themselves (SMARCE1→SMARCB1/SMARCA4, SMARCB1→CDKN2A/GLI1, MEIS3→SHH, PRDM10→CDKN2A, POU6F2→CDKN2A), so the module is nameable and partly placed. But no retrieved paper connects SMARCB1, SMARCE1, MEIS3, PRDM10 or POU6F2 to COVID-19 — the SMARCB1 papers that were retrieved are explicitly off-topic (sarcoma) — so the COVID-19 side of the story rests on reasoning, not retrieval, keeping this short of 'supported.'
support: PMID 39177582 — places YAP1 as a driver in a preclinical sarcoma/cancer model, consistent with an oncogenic proliferation role; PMID 36479120 — YAP1 pan-cancer role in survival prediction and immune modulation; PMID 34719224 — YAP1 as prognostic biomarker correlated with telomerase across cancers; PMID 34257617 — YAP1 gene regulatory network as prognostic biomarker across human cancers. No retrieved PMID places SMARCB1, SMARCE1, MEIS3, PRDM10 or POU6F2 in either disease, and none place any carrying factor in COVID-19.
how_to_falsify: In matched severe-vs-mild COVID-19 PBMC or endothelial datasets, test whether SMARCB1/SMARCE1 (BAF) occupancy and YAP1 activity co-vary with CDKN2A/p16 induction and senescence markers; no such coordination would refute the COVID-19 side. In LGG models, knock down SMARCB1/SMARCE1 in glioma-stem cells and test whether CDKN2A is de-repressed via loss of GLI1/YAP1-driven silencing; if CDKN2A regulation is unaffected, the module does not carry the effect this account claims.
caveats: Blood and brain are mechanistically distant tissues, and the concordant factors here sit at 40-53% of the 124 available patient-group comparisons (48/124-66/124), not near-universal agreement, drawn from only 4 independent cohort pairs. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed the classic immune/hematopoietic regulators (GFI1, NFATC1, LEF1, KLF2, SPIB, LITAF, SMAD3, TCF4, CREB5, HLX, EGR4, SREBF2) that a straightforward 'COVID-19 = immune activation' story would have used, so this account deliberately avoids an interferon/immune narrative. The single-view list (RBPJ/Notch, E2F8, SIRT1, ZHX2, etc.) shows several plausible cell-cycle/stem-signaling factors scored high in only one patient subgroup and were correctly excluded rather than folded into the story.
